signatures.description: Symptom: `hilo graph module no/such/dir` printed a success-shaped empty report (Files: 0 / Edges: 0 / Tests: 0.0%) and exited 0, indistinguishable from a real but empty module, while sibling subcommands `graph related <path>` and `graph impact <path>` already failed loudly (exit 1, "not in the graph"). Fix that worked: classify the prefix against the filesystem BEFORE the graph-db resolution (clap positional, no flag change) into UnknownPrefix / UncoveredDirectory in a private pure helper so the decision is unit-testable without DuckDB; on UnknownPrefix return anyhow::anyhow!("'{prefix}' is not in the graph (no such directory and no matching module prefix)") at BOTH the no-graph path and the empty-stats path (so a fresh unwarmed tree answers a typo with the prefix error, not "No graph data"), and keep the tolerant case (directory deleted after a warm, graph still names files under the prefix) reporting normally. For a real directory with zero graph coverage keep exit 0 but print an UNCONDITIONAL, state-independent line: "No files in the graph under '<prefix>' - the directory exists but no warmed graph entry covers it. Run `hilo graph warm`." Evidence: exit 1 naming the prefix from the repo root and from a fresh mktemp dir with no .vfs; `hilo-graph/src` still exit 0 with Files 13 / Edges 79 byte-identical to pre-fix; `--help` unchanged; new unit tests classify_empty_module_unknown_prefix / classify_empty_module_uncovered_directory plus an integration test running the built binary in a temp dir. Pitfall for the foreman: do NOT put RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check in a local gate brief on this host - the flag changes the dependency fingerprint and recompiles libduckdb-sys C++ from source (~26 min); the repo's own scripts/rust-lint.sh (clippy -D warnings) plus CI cover that leg.
